content.title: About
content.content: Corn squares are dry cereal made from whole corn, formed into small square pieces. They are crunchy, mildly sweet, and commonly enjoyed as a quick breakfast or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn squares first appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as an alternative to wheat cereals.
The square shape is convenient for portion control and is often used in children's meals.
Their fiber content is higher than that of most traditional rice cereals.
The corn used is typically non‑GMO in European production.
Corn squares are frequently fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn squares provide sustained energy through slow release of glucose.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and helps maintain normal cholesterol levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack cereals, corn squares contain almost no fat.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and niacin aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Corn is naturally gluten‑free, making the product suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Some varieties are sweetened, increasing their calorie count.

items.title: Possible PET residues
items.content: Packaging may involve PET, which can leave microscopic residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn squares can be eaten dry, added to milk, yogurt or kefir. They are often used in children's meals, as a base for granola bars, or as a crunchy element in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place in an airtight container. For long‑term storage, keep in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent moisture.

coffee-iced-latte-with-non-dairy-milk-fl.title: Coffee Iced Latte with Non-Dairy Milk, Flavored

content.title: About
content.content: Iced latte is a cold coffee drink made with espresso, ice, and plant‑based milk (soy, almond, oat, etc.). The flavored version adds a syrup such as vanilla, caramel, or hazelnut for extra taste. It is popular in warm weather and suitable for those avoiding dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Iced latte originated in Japan in the 1980s as a response to the growing demand for cold coffee beverages.
Plant‑based milks lower the saturated‑fat content compared with cow’s milk.
Flavor syrups are often derived from natural extracts but can also contain artificial components.
Cold coffee retains most of the antioxidants found in hot espresso.
Common flavor options include vanilla, caramel, honey, coconut, and hazelnut.

items.title: Caffeine boost
items.content: Espresso provides caffeine, which can increase alertness and improve concentration.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals in the body.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Using plant‑based milk makes the drink suitable for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee contains niacin, riboflavin, and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The large proportion of water and ice contributes to overall fluid intake.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after caffeine.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored syrups are often sweetened, increasing the drink’s calorie count.

items.title: Allergy to plant milk
items.content: Soy, almond, or other plant milks can trigger allergic reactions in susceptible people.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee’s natural acidity may irritate the stomach of those with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the iced latte in tall glasses over ice, adding the chosen flavored syrup. Top with plant‑based whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon or cocoa powder if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared drink should be kept refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours. Store unopened plant‑based milk in its original container, tightly sealed, at 1‑4 °C.

white-pizza-cheese-thick-crust.title: White Pizza with Cheese, Thick Crust

content.title: About
content.content: White pizza with cheese and a thick crust is a classic Italian pizza without tomato sauce, topped with a generous layer of mozzarella, parmesan, and sometimes ricotta. The dough is made from flour, water, yeast, and salt, then shaped into a thick, soft yet crispy crust that holds the aromatic cheese blend.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional “white” pizza originated in Naples as an alternative to tomato‑based pies when tomatoes were seasonal.
The cheese blend often combines several varieties to achieve a more complex flavor and texture.
A thick crust requires a longer bake, resulting in a puffier interior and a crunchy exterior.
Some regions add garlic, olive oil, and herbs (oregano, basil) to enhance the aroma.
White pizza is usually served without additional sauces, letting the cheese shine.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheeses used are rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Mozzarella and parmesan provide complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamin B12 content
items.content: Dairy cheeses supply vitamin B12, supporting nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic potential (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Certain aged cheeses, like parmesan, may contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of a thick crust and cheese delivers lasting fullness, helping to curb snacking.

items.title: High calorie count
items.content: The thick dough and abundant cheese make this pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheeses contain saturated fats, which can affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may need lactose‑free cheeses or alternatives.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the white pizza hot, sliced into individual portions. Fresh arugula, shaved parmesan, or a drizzle of balsamic glaze add a bright contrast. It can be eaten with hands or with a knife and fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.
